question.text: Which statement about Category III AIFs is CORRECT in the context of investment strategies?

answer.text: Cat III AIFs can take leverage and derivative positions to generate absolute returns over medium-to-long term.
Cat III AIFs cannot invest in derivatives.
Cat III AIFs must only invest intra-day.
Cat III AIFs are restricted to equity long-only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs may take leverage, short positions and derivative positions in order to generate absolute returns over the medium and long term, and generally are not intended for intra-day trading. The Trap: Saying Cat III AIFs cannot invest in derivatives, must only invest intra-day, or are restricted to equity long-only contradicts the source description of their permitted strategies. Note: The defining feature is the combination of permitted leverage, short positions and derivative positions for medium-to-long-term absolute returns.
